chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the night prayer: do I pray it at the beginning of the night? He said, 'Yes, I do that. And if the camel-driver hurries me, I pray it in the saddle (on the camel-drawn litter).'

key_terms.الْجَمَّالُ: Camel-driver / one who drives the camel

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray the night prayer while riding a camel if time is short?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility of Salat al-Layl, affirming its performance at the start of the night while accommodating the practical realities of travel. The Imam’s mention of praying in the saddle (*mahmil*) when hurried by the camel-driver underscores the principle of *rukhas* (dispensations) in Shia jurisprudence, allowing for abbreviated prayers in motion when time is constrained. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with the ease (*yusr*) granted to believers in varying circumstances.
